name: UR RTDE joint servo motion example
summary: SDU Robotics Python example that connects an RTDE control interface, moves to an initial joint target and repeatedly sends sinusoidal six-joint servoJ targets. Importing or running the original script can start physical motion; this reference supplies inert source metadata only.

license.scope: Selected ur_rtde example source code under the pinned repository MIT license. Preserve its copyright and permission notice, including Anders Prier Lindvig - SDU Robotics. Third-party dependencies, robot firmware, URCaps and hardware retain their own applicable terms.

hardware: Operator-authorized UR robot/controller with a configured RTDE endpoint; model and software versions are unverified
system: Network access to the intended RTDE controller endpoint
An operator-reviewed Python environment for the pinned source and its bindings
requirements.notes: This straight-line script constructs RTDEControlInterface with an embedded loopback address and calls moveJ before entering its try/finally block. A loopback address does not establish a simulator environment. Inspect and adapt the address, six-joint start target, sinusoidal amplitudes/frequencies/phases, lookahead and gain for the authorized installation. The loop uses dt=1/500 seconds with initPeriod, servoJ and waitPeriod; this is a requested control period, not measured real-time or 500 Hz performance. It continues until interruption or another exception. The finally block calls servoStop and stopScript after leaving that loop; startup operations occur before it. The pinned README provides project-level installation and robot/OS declarations; no Python/package version, controller, firmware, robot, operating-system or timing combination was resolved or tested for this source.

invocation.notes: Upstream invocation only after separate operator authorization and configuration. There is no main guard, and executing or importing the file can connect and move hardware. The source defines an indefinite servo loop and does not verify reachability, collision safety or real-time scheduling. The Hub supplies no execution/preparation adapter. No upstream execution, controller contact, simulator or package installation was performed during source review.
